questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Estonia?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Estonia article.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Estonia?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Estonia on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Estonia article.

questions.proof: Estonia has borders with Sweden, Finland, Russia and Latvia.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Estonia?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “History” part of the Estonia article.

questions.proof: The occupied country was called the Estonian Soviet Socialist Republic by the Soviets.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Since administrative reform in _____, there are in total 79 local governments.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twenty-first century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Administrative regions” part of the Estonia article.

questions.proof: Since administrative reform in 2017, there are in total 79 local governments.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Estonia won the War of Independence (1918-1920) against Soviet _____.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “Soviet”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Estonia article, under the heading “History”.

questions.proof: Estonia won the War of Independence (1918-1920) against Soviet Russia.
